title: Qt: DisplayFilterEdit touch-ups
description:
Don't draw the DisplayFilterEdit right line if there aren't any
buttons to separate from the filter text area.
    
Don't use the bookmarks on the display filter expression dialog,
which is read-only, and only responds to GUI clicks.

Signal that the display filter list has changed when removing
a bookmark, so that all DFE bookmarks update (to change the
icon color.)

Update the bookmark menu before showing it, which helps keep the
list in sync without worrying as much about signaling from one
to another.

Fixup !16002

No immediate success, this also ruined the main display filter background.
* Main display filter background does not fill the rectangle
* The rounded corner is not correct, looks like the corner is missing
* The separate line does not look good because it's 1px into the border (the color is different than the border)
* The find display filter background is 1px into the bookmark button

![Screenshot_2024-07-12_at_18.55.03](/uploads/598ce1e95d31ddfecaf36a825d4c1ab2/Screenshot_2024-07-12_at_18.55.03.png)

> Main display filter background does not fill the rectangle

Having a border makes
`style()->subElementRect(QStyle::SE_LineEditContents, &opt, this);` smaller (even though the border is not drawn when embedded in a QComboBox). Possible to work around.

> The find display filter background is 1px into the bookmark button

That can be fixed relatively easily.

> The separate line does not look good because it's 1px into the border (the color is different than the border)

I think the color being different on macOS is because of the special `QLineEdit` style sheet applied in `accordion_frame.cpp` for macOS. The rounded corner gets created even with the other border there too. Those can probably be worked around, but it's not easy to control the separator line color because it's not easy to retrieve "whatever the current style sheet says the border should be for this Widget."

Possible more in-depth approaches:

1. Just use DisplayFilterCombo everywhere. Probably need to change the global for the filter history or at least take a look at it.
2. We already draw the background a second time manually for SyntaxFilterEdit to deal with how Qt 6 (and 5.15.x) deals with QLineEdit embedded in QComboBox. Maybe that could be the only way we draw the background, and we set the normal background to transparent or something.
3. Maybe the adding of QActions with QIcons to QLineEdits has gotten better in the last 8 or 10 years and we don't need `StockIconToolButton` anymore?

It's fairly difficult to figure out the correct color to draw the border line, because different styles and themes draw the line edit border differently by default (including different colors and thickness for selected vs non-selected). I'm tempted to just not set the border color and not draw the left vertical line at all.

If we do still draw it, then decreasing the height by the frame width would presumably fix make it at least not be into the border. But no line might look better than a slightly different line.

!16405 just doesn't draw it at all. It also makes the icon left border curved with the same radius so that the rounded corner looks better. (Looks like there's some small bleed of the highlight color at the corners when the syntax status changes, which might be slightly better with some rounding.)

The color of the separator line is not an issue, it looks good. The problem here is the several off-by-one pixel issues we have now, the separator line should be one/two pixels shorter to fit into the frame, not drawing over the frame.

I'll suggest we revert the last commits, including adding the bookmark button, and work on a good solution for this before merging more fixes.

commits_data.title: Qt: DisplayFilterEdit bookmark button background
commits_data.message:
Qt: DisplayFilterEdit bookmark button background

Make the DisplayFilterEdit have the same border (and border color)
as the vertical dividing line between the bookmark button and the
filter, just as the DisplayFilterCombo does.

Add a tiny margin to the button style, so that the 1px border from
the DisplayFilterEdit shows up even if the button background is
not transparent. Make the button background be that of the line
edit, so that it doesn't get overriden with the syntax colors.

Followup to !16002
